findings.title: SPN-registered service accounts with passwords never rotated
findings.correlation_note: svc-sql01, svc-web01, svc-backup all appear in Act 3's Kerberoasting TGS burst — see .pristine/ad/kerberos-events.txt and spn-listing.txt.
findings.detail: All three have SPNs registered and passwords last set 900+ days ago — Kerberoastable by any authenticated domain user with no elevated access required.
findings.recommended_fix: Rotate service account passwords on a schedule (or migrate to gMSA where possible) and use long, random passwords resistant to offline cracking.

findings.title: Service account with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled
findings.correlation_note: svc-legacyapp is equally exposed (AS-REP roastable) but ad/kerberos-events.txt found no matching 4768-without-preauth event in the incident window — this exposure was not confirmed as used by the attacker, unlike AD-1.
findings.detail: 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' is set, meaning an AS-REP ticket can be requested and cracked offline with no valid credentials at all.
findings.recommended_fix: Re-enable Kerberos pre-authentication unless there is a specific, documented legacy-application requirement; if required, isolate the account's permissions to the minimum needed and rotate its password.
